title: Feasibility Study: Sonographic Estimation of Respiratory Effort Using Diaphragm Thickening for Titration of Pressure Support in Non-Invasive Ventilation
summary:
This study aims to investigate whether ultrasound measurements of the diaphragm can help doctors select the appropriate pressure support for patients receiving mask ventilation due to acute respiratory failure. The diaphragm is an important respiratory muscle, and its thickening during breathing can provide an indication of how much effort the patient has to exert when breathing.

In the study, 60 patients will be randomly assigned either to the intervention group, where pressure support is selected based on ultrasound measurements, or to the standard-of-care group, where the treating medical team determines the settings. The study will primarily assess whether this approach is feasible and can be reliably implemented, including recruitment, adherence to study procedures and the completeness of the data collected.

The study will also collect preliminary information on safety and clinical outcomes, including mask ventilation failure, complications and mortality. The results will help determine whether a larger study should be conducted to establish whether ultrasound-guided mask ventilation can improve the treatment of patients with acute respiratory failure.

interventions.name:
In the control group, ΔP insp is chosen based on standard practice. 
All further measures and the total duration of treatment are also determined in accordance with standard practice.

In the intervention group, ΔP insp is chosen based on the DTF measurements determined during an initial titration sequence. The ΔP insp level with the lowest associated DTF will be chosen for the first 24 hours of NIV.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients (aged ≥ 18 years) with acute respiratory failure where NIV is indicated (e.g. hypoxemia, hypercapnia, exacerbation of COPD or pneumonia)
Exclusion criteria:
- Presence of a do-not-intubate order
- Uncontrollable agitation or restlessness
- Known diaphragmatic dysfunction
- Insurmountable obstacle to performing an ultrasound to measure DTF (e.g. large wounds and/or dressings).
- Current pregnancy
